newsitem.title: JAPAN: China says gasoline stations increasing rapidly.
newsitem.headline: China says gasoline stations increasing rapidly.

text.p: The number of gasoline stations in China has surged in the 10 years to 1995, an official of China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) told an industry symposium in Tokyo on Wednesday.
"Statistics indicate that service stations multiplied 40 times from only 2,000 in 1985 to 80,000 in 1995," said Han Gang, vice-president of the state-owned oil firm.
He said a large majority of the stations, some of which are owned by the state, opened after 1991.

Demand for petroleum products was currently rising at a high pace of five percent a year, he told the symposium on modernisation of the petroleum industry being attended by oil industry officials from 18 countries.
With transportation of petroleum products heavily dependent on and burdening long-distance railways, efforts were being made to increase offshore transportation, he said.
Port facilities were being enhanced and oil tanks being built in southern coastal cities, he said.
He said railways transported 64 percent of petroleum products transported. The rest was mainly transported by ship, with only a small amount moved by pipeline or truck.
